name: Spike - does offline Assetto Corsa run the clock at x48
notes: Shortening a race speeds its clock up by the same step, so a 24-hour race run at 1/48 of its laps still goes through the night - and the largest step sends TIME_MULT=48. Nothing has measured whether offline AC honours a multiplier that high, where it stops honouring one, or whether the clock carries on past midnight. MAX_TIME_MULTIPLIER in src/shared/utils/race-scale is 48 until this says otherwise. THE CONTROLLER IS NAMED ON PURPOSE: base is CSP's own static controller, and a dynamic one would get in the way - both PURE and Sol set the game's clock to their plan's multiplier while a plan plays, so under either this probe would measure the planner rather than AC. spikes/time-multiplier-plan is the probe for that. PROCEDURE: `npm run race -- spikes/time-multiplier`, drive out of the pits and watch the time of day - CSP's own clock in the pit menu or any time app will do, or failing that the sky. It starts at 22:00. WHAT HAS TO BE TRUE at x48: a game hour passes every 75 seconds, so the clock reads about 23:00 at 75 seconds in, midnight at 2.5 minutes, 04:00 at 7.5 minutes and 06:00 at 10 minutes - the session runs 12, so the last of those is inside it. IF THE CLOCK RUNS SLOWER than that, the multiplier is capped below 48: note how far it got in a timed minute, which is the cap, and set MAX_TIME_MULTIPLIER to it. IF IT STOPS AT MIDNIGHT, or jumps back, the night of a 24-hour race cannot be crossed in one launch and that goes into Known gaps. IF IT RUNS AT 48 AND CARRIES ON past midnight, the provisional cap stands and the note in constants.ts can say it was measured.
